items.title: Mid-Year Budget Review: Deloitte Africa Executive calls for better revenue mobilisation and focused flagship programmes
items.description: Partner and Africa Leader for Infrastructure, Capital Projects and Real Estate at Deloitte Africa, Yaw Appiah Lartey, has welcomed aspects of the government’s Mid-Year Budget Review, particularly measures aimed at improving the financing of capital projects, while urging authorities to strengthen revenue mobilisation and avoid duplication in the implementation of flagship programmes. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, Mr Appiah Lartey said Ghana’s economic recovery efforts must go beyond expenditure controls and focus on sustainable revenue generation, efficient project financing and targeted interventions. His comments come after the Finance Minister’s Mid-Year Budget Review highlighted falling inflation, a stronger cedi, improved fiscal discipline and renewed confidence in the economy. However, the Minority in Parliament has argued that the positive macroeconomic indicators do not fully reflect challenges such as reduced spending, delays in implementing flagship programmes and questions over government priorities. Mr Appiah Lartey said one of the longstanding challenges with public infrastructure projects has been the absence of dedicated funding arrangements before projects begin, resulting in stalled works and accumulated debts owed to contractors. “There may be some concern that has been raised. The first is that, historically, some of our capital expenditures have not had earmarked funds. We incur them and we have issues with contractors not being paid,” he said. He described the move towards ensuring that projects have identified funding sources before implementation as a positive step. “For me, this is positive because you have a situation where the construction starts, it gets stuck in the middle of the way and there’s no fund debt,” he stated. According to him, establishing a financing framework for projects would prevent situations where government begins construction only to search for funding after work has commenced. “You will have to have some form of sinking fund for the debts that we are incurring for the programmes that we plan. So it’s a positive thing, in my view, because a project starts and doesn’t have to get to the middle before we start looking for funding,” he added. The Deloitte executive said while government’s efforts to control expenditure were important, more attention should be paid to revenue generation. He noted that although government missed its revenue target, the shortfall was relatively small, and the focus should now shift towards improving areas where Ghana has historically underperformed. “We should also look at the revenue aspect. So yes, there’s been some control on expenditure, but on the revenue side, we missed our target, albeit about 1.1%, which is good,” he said. Mr Appiah Lartey argued that Ghana has often focused on introducing new taxes while failing to maximise existing revenue sources, particularly property taxation. “We kept introducing new taxes, not mentioning e-levy, forgetting that we had low-hanging fruit,” he said. He welcomed efforts to improve property tax collection, noting that making property bills more accessible could help increase compliance. “Now property bills come to your home like ECG bills. That’s an important development because we are focusing on what we have been taxing over the years, forgetting that they are low-hanging fruit,” he said. He questioned whether Ghana could improve revenue performance by expanding property taxation rather than continuously introducing new levies. “We keep talking about widening the tax net, but this was low-hanging fruit, property taxes. Can we outperform that?” he asked. Mr Appiah Lartey also highlighted corporate income taxes and oil revenues as areas that require closer attention. “If corporate income taxes are increasing, then it means that there’s production going on,” he said. He called for stronger systems to capture economic activities taking place online, particularly transactions involving non-resident digital platforms. “There are people who are making money in Ghana here using online. How are you tracking them? Can you make business or make money from the United States online without being taxed? If elsewhere you cannot do that easily, then we should also look at it,” he said. The Deloitte executive also argued that Ghana should maximise the benefits of the national identification system by linking the Ghana Card to tax compliance. “We have gone through the rigorous process of registering Ghanaians. We should be able to tax them,” he said. He noted that the Ghana Card is already required for several services and argued that tax compliance should be integrated into that system. “It applies in the courts. It applies in the bank. You need a Ghana Card to do everything. Why don’t we follow that up to ensure that everybody who has a Ghana Card, any Ghanaian who has a Ghana Card, is tax compliant?” he asked. He pointed to tax compliance practices in countries such as the United States, where citizens are required to file tax returns, as an example Ghana could consider. Mr Appiah Lartey welcomed proposed tax reforms, including the planned review of income tax legislation and adjustments to VAT registration thresholds. He said some tax laws had become outdated and needed to reflect current economic realities. He supported the increase in the VAT registration threshold from GH¢250 to GH¢750, arguing that the previous threshold was no longer appropriate. “GH¢250 was many years ago. And today, a trader making GH¢250 is still like someone in a shop or a container. You don’t put that person through the cost of trying to register for VAT. You have to increase that,” he said. He also welcomed proposed reforms to excise duties, particularly the planned removal of the 20% excise duty on locally manufactured food products, saying it could help local industries compete with imported goods. Mr Appiah Lartey criticised the duplication of government initiatives, arguing that some flagship programmes have struggled because they create new structures instead of strengthening existing institutions. He cited programmes such as One District, One Factory and One Village, One Dam, saying some challenges were linked to the creation of separate secretariats alongside existing ministries and agencies. “There are a number of problems with those initiatives, which doesn’t make them successful. One is that we duplicate them. We duplicate existing institutions and agencies,” he said. “Why would you have a One District, One Factory secretariat when you have a Ministry of Trade and Industry? They have all the data. They have all the resources to run it,” he added. According to him, creating parallel structures can lead to delays and institutional conflicts. “We create a secretariat. So we spent about two years creating a policy and office initiative to run the department. Then we have, my entrepreneurship lecturer will say, six months of power play. The minister fights with the CEO of the secretariat. And then another three months of injury time after the fight,” he said. He urged government to rely more on existing institutions and agencies instead of establishing new administrative bodies for every major initiative. Mr Appiah Lartey also called for a more focused approach to the government’s proposed 24-hour economy programme, warning that broad initiatives may struggle without clear sector priorities. “My problem with some of these initiatives is that they are expansive and too wide. Let’s focus on sectors where we can make transformation happen,” he said. He cited the Cassava Starch Initiative under former President John Agyekum Kufuor as an example of a targeted intervention linked to a specific industrial objective. “President Kufuor started the Cassava Starch initiative and there was a factory established to support that,” he said. On the 24-hour economy policy, he asked: “What are the key sectors that we are focusing on and how are we making them function to optimise the benefits?” Mr Appiah Lartey said initiatives such as the Women’s Development Bank should also be implemented effectively while avoiding unnecessary duplication of existing institutions.

items.title: Russie-Kazakhstan : Poutine et Tokaïev prônent l'IA et le numérique pour révolutionner le transport eurasien
items.description: Le president russe Vladimir Poutine, aux cotes de son homologue kazakh Kassym-Jomart Tokaïev, a pris la parole ce 25 juillet lors de la seance pleniere du forum sur la cooperation interregionale entre la Russie et le Kazakhstan, qui s'est tenu a Omsk, en Siberie. Au cours de son intervention, le dirigeant russe a souligne que la Russie et le Kazakhstan etaient a l'avant-garde de la mise en œuvre de projets communs dans le cadre de l'Union economique eurasienne (UEE). Le chef de l'etat russe a notamment evoque la possibilite de recourir a l'intelligence artificielle pour mettre en place des chaînes de transport optimales. Vladimir Poutine a egalement souligne les vastes perspectives d'un renforcement continu de la cooperation mutuellement benefique dans des domaines tels que les transports, la logistique, l'economie et la vie sociale. Il a souligne que les echanges commerciaux entre la Russie et le Kazakhstan s'elevaient en 2025 a pres de 29 milliards de dollars, tandis que le volume des investissements russes dans l'economie kazakhe avait depasse la barre des 30 milliards de dollars. Par ailleurs, Vladimir Poutine a mis en avant la cooperation active dans le developpement de la liaison de transport internationale Nord-Sud. Selon lui, la croissance des livraisons sur cette liaison a atteint 10 % au cours des cinq premiers mois de l'annee 2026. Le president russe a ajoute que la frequence et la couverture geographique des vols entre la Russie et le Kazakhstan s'accroissaient, et que l'ouverture de liaisons aeriennes entre Orenbourg et Almaty etait prevue prochainement. La Russie et le Kazakhstan s'efforcent d'augmenter la capacite d'accueil des terminaux de transit et des postes-frontieres situes a leur frontiere commune, a indique Vladimir Poutine. Il a egalement annonce la signature d'une serie de nouveaux accords, memorandums et contrats commerciaux. La Russie et le Kazakhstan sont d'importants partenaires commerciaux, affirme Tokaïev Kassym-Jomart Tokaïev a quant a lui souligne le niveau sans precedent atteint par les relations entre la Russie et le Kazakhstan. Selon lui, les deux pays sont d'importants partenaires commerciaux et les tendances dans ce domaine sont positives. Le dirigeant kazakh s'est egalement dit convaincu que, grâce a la confiance mutuelle, les deux parties connaîtront de nouveaux succes. Dans son discours, Kassym-Jomart Tokaïev a propose de lancer le corridor de transport numerique Kazakhstan–Russie, se declarant convaincu qu'une integration numerique efficace des systemes de transport et de logistique des deux pays, ainsi que l'utilisation a grande echelle des nouvelles technologies, permettront d'accroître le volume des echanges commerciaux bilateraux, d'augmenter les flux de transit et de renforcer globalement les liens economiques. Le XXIIe Forum de cooperation interregionale entre la Russie et le Kazakhstan se tient a Omsk les 24 et 25 juillet. Avant la seance pleniere du forum, Vladimir Poutine s'est entretenu avec Kassym-Jomart Tokaïev, avec lequel il a discute des relations commerciales et economiques entre leurs deux pays, ainsi que du conflit en Ukraine.

items.title: Fleeing a wall of flames: Tourists describe France wildfires escape
items.description: Tourists told the BBC of emergency alerts in the middle of the night, desperate drives just metres from six-storey high flames and the sight of people flocking to beaches with their suitcases. Huge forest fires in south-west France and central Spain have displaced more than 220,000 people, with the French military drafted in to help and the Spanish government declaring a national emergency. Winds and continued heat are still helping to fan the flames with some tourists reporting smelling acrid smoke like a “bonfire” far outside the affected areas. Flights to Bordeaux and Madrid, the closest cities to the blaze-hit regions, are currently not affected. Earlier on Saturday, a French foreign minister described the fires as a “tragedy” but urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans. Among those caught up in the crisis is Zac Morrison, who arrived in Cap Ferret – a popular peninsula blanketed with pine trees 40 miles (65km) south-west of Bordeaux – on Thursday. The 21-year-old from London, who is on holiday with 10 members of his family, woke up to two text alerts at 04:00 and 06:00 local time ordering him to evacuate “by all means necessary”. “We had the gendarmerie [French military] going door to door,” he told BBC Your Voice. “It was something like out of a movie – we had to take everything.” Since experiencing “panic” before a “well organised” operation to clear out the entire peninsula, he said he received four different evacuation alerts from the authorities – the most recent at 17:00 on Friday – after “we moved away from one fire to only get put into the crosshairs of another”. His family took shelter on a beach in nearby Arcachon before a relative came to their aid with a place to stay. His brother Nate, 11, is still coming to terms with having seen the flames. “Other people have been sleeping in schools and warehouses and the beaches have had people just waiting for the go ahead,” Morrison added. “There’s people on the beach here with their suitcases.” He said the family was awaiting instructions on whether they can continue their holiday until mid August. “It rained last night but we are hearing that electricity may be cut out over the peninsula, especially as the ash clouds go towards Bordeaux… I’ve heard about houses burning in just an hour, it’s scary but sadly people here are getting used to it.” Family fled in 15 minutes David Morton had enjoyed most of his week-long trip to Cap Ferret with his wife and two teenage sons in the forests under baking sun. But the mixture of “tinder dry” pine and intense heat helped upend things on day five when the family was awoken on Friday morning. “Our phones were all flashing and bleeping; there was a message saying we had to evacuate immediately and drive on the one road out of the [Cap Ferret] peninsula,” he said. “We literally threw everything into our suitcases and within 15 minutes were in the hire car.” He said they came within 500m of the main fire. “The flames were higher than full-size forest pine trees, so five or six storeys high, and it was clear this was a fire that was out of control at that point.” The family has stayed with friends until their flight home from Bordeaux on Saturday. ‘City is evacuated but I’m still here’ Others are still stranded. Rebecca Papin, a French-American visiting her holiday home in the commune of Biscarrosse, near to the Cap Ferret peninsula, saw a large plume of smoke in the distance on Thursday. Just three hours later when she arrived home that night, “there were water planes in the sky dropping water, firefighter helicopters in the sky and the entire distance was just a wall of flames,” she told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. “It was quite far away from my house but I could see it very clearly from the upstairs level of my home.” She said the authorities appeared “overwhelmed with trying” to fight the fire and issued no evacuation order, so she slept alongside her young children with her earplugs in – meaning she missed the sound of the evacuation overnight. “When I woke up in the morning we were almost alone in the city because the city has been evacuated and I’m still here,” she said. “The main roads are closed because they’re on fire – the police advised me on Friday at 07:30 to stay in my home, to not leave my home under any circumstance; there was ash falling from the sky like snow.” Some British families told the BBC they had moved 100 miles away to other parts of France to continue their holidays. Mark Dorey, from Leeds, decided to drive to the Dordogne with his wife and three children after being evacuated from a campsite near Parentis-en-Born. “You wouldn’t believe it, but me and my two boys were watching a Queen tribute act at the campsite bar – straight after a rendition of Bohemian Rhapsody someone stopped them to say we were being evacuated at about 22:00,” he said. Before heading to the Dordogne the family spent a night with hundreds of other evacuees in a gymnasium. He said he feels lucky to be looked after and safe, but is thinking about holidaying “closer to home” next year. And BBC South’s Joanna Kent, who was on holiday in the Cap Ferret peninsula earlier this week, recalled seeing her campsite deserted after two van loads of police told tourists they had 30 minutes to get out. While the wildfires show no sign of abating soon, the UK Foreign Office is currently not advising against travel to France or Spain. Éléonore Caroit, France’s minister for international partnerships, advised tourists on Saturday: “You have entire areas that are fine, you’re seeing similar phenomena in Spain and other countries. “I’m in Paris and nothing is happening, and most other regions are OK, so do please come to France and do not cancel your travel plans. “But wherever you are, please do be advised as to what might be happening.” In Madrid the fires are in the wider region far outside the city centre – and authorities are battling to stop different fires merging. But the flames have already shut down a facility for US space agency Nasa 37 miles (65km) west of the city. Madrid’s regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the fire there as the “worst fire in the history of the region”, with the area facing a “perfect storm” of high temperatures, relentless wind and merging fire fronts.

items.title: Nobody should have reason to doubt Peter Obi’s one-term promise — Kwankwaso
items.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will honour his pledge to serve only one term if elected in the 2027 presidential election. Kwankwaso stated this during an interview on News Central’s 60 Minutes with Mr Kay while responding to questions about Obi’s commitment to a single four-year tenure and whether he would seek the presidency after the proposed arrangement. According to him, Obi has publicly made the promise and should be trusted to keep his word. “I personally believe Peter Obi is a gentleman and I have every reason to trust him, especially that he said it to the hearing of everybody. Nobody should have any reason to doubt him,” Kwankwaso said. He explained that the power-sharing arrangement within the NDC was built on mutual trust and a collective agreement among the coalition partners. Kwankwaso also argued that allowing the South to complete an eight-year tenure aligns with the understanding reached by members of the alliance. “We believe the southern part of the country should complete its second term and with that, and to the hearing of everybody in this country, I don’t believe any gentleman would want to renege, would want to say no or change his or her mind,” he stated. The former Kano State governor added that beyond individual ambitions, the coalition had developed a shared roadmap for governance that would guide whoever eventually leads the country. According to him, the NDC’s focus is on implementing its agreed agenda rather than advancing the interests of any particular political bloc. “More importantly, we have collectively gotten a short-term, medium-term and, of course, long-term plan for this country. It does not matter whether it is him from the Obidient side, or my humble self from the Kwankwasiyya side or another side, we believe we have an agenda,” he said. Kwankwaso stressed that the coalition would work to ensure continuity of its programmes regardless of who occupies the presidency in the future. “That agenda, we will as much as possible ensure that whoever comes, maybe Peter, maybe me or any other person, would stick to that programme,” he added. items.title: Abacha: Don’t tell lies about the dead, Al-Mustapha tells ex-DSS officer
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief Security Officer to late Head of State, General Sani Abacha, Major Hamza Al-Mustapha, has dismissed claims made by a former Department of State Services (DSS) operative, Mr. Amachree, regarding the final moments of the late military ruler, describing the account as false. Read Also: No, Abacha didn’t die in bed with a woman Speaking with journalists in Kaduna, Al-Mustapha said the claims contained in the former DSS official’s book were untrue, alleging that the author was influenced by others to write them. “The boy was asked to write the lies by others. I have all the CCTV footages of what happened in my custody, so what he said are not true,” Al-Mustapha said. He maintained that the account presented in the publication did not reflect what transpired, insisting that he possessed evidence to contradict the assertions made about Abacha’s death. Al-Mustapha further urged the public to disregard the claims, saying it was wrong to make what he described as false statements against someone who was no longer alive to respond. “Just ignore his lies. It’s bad to say such things on someone that is dead,” he said. What the ex-DSS officer wrote According to Amachree’s story: ”At approximately 2.40 a.m., shortly after Gen. Useni left, Abacha’s girlfriend, an Igbo lady (name withheld), arrived at the Aso Rock Guest House from the Nicon Noga Hilton Hotel,” excerpts from the book read. “With her was her younger sister, a pharmacist who was in Abuja for a conference. The Head of State had just bought his girlfriend a new SUV, and they decided to stop by to say hello to ‘Oga’. “Abacha was taken with the younger sister, and after a short while, the girlfriend returned to the hotel, leaving the pharmacist alone with the Head of State. “At about 4.05 a.m., as they were getting intimate, the pharmacist realized Abacha had stopped moving. She called out to him, but he was unresponsive and stiff. She checked his pulse; there was none. “In a state of panic, she quickly dressed and left the guest house, telling the soldier in guard duty that ‘Oga’ had asked for a car to take her back to her hotel. “The soldier, unaware of the gravity of the situation, promptly arranged for her transportation. She returned to the Hilton, and after telling her sister what had happened, was quickly driven to the Abuja Airport to catch the 7 a.m., Okada Airline flight to Lagos.” Then Amachree interrogated the pharmacist in Lagos, as the DSS Director of Operations at the national headquarters, Abuja, instructed him: “The first thing she said to me was: ‘I did not kill him, he died on top of me.” Then Amachree contacted the Director of National Operations in Abuja and dispatched the lady back to Abuja immediately. The post Abacha: Don’t tell lies about the dead, Al-Mustapha tells ex-DSS officer appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: WACI demands FG, Ondo govt intervention over Iru–Imesi road
items.description: By Nnasom David The War Against Corruption Initiative International (WACI) has raised concerns over the deteriorating condition of the Iru–Imesi Road in Ondo State, describing the situation as a humanitarian and economic crisis requiring urgent government intervention. The organisation’s Director of Operations, Thomas Kahinde, made the call after experiencing firsthand the difficulties faced by motorists, commuters, traders and residents who use the route. Kahinde said what was expected to be a routine journey through the road turned into several hours of frustration after vehicular movement was brought to a standstill due to the poor condition of the road. He said he was forced to leave his vehicle to investigate the cause of the prolonged gridlock, where he discovered that the road had remained in a deplorable state for an extended period. According to him, interactions with residents, transport operators and other road users revealed that although the road project had reportedly been awarded, the contractor handling the project had not been adequately mobilised to commence substantial work. He lamented that commercial buses, private vehicles and trucks conveying goods had been left stranded for hours, leaving passengers exhausted and uncertain about when they would reach their destinations. Kahinde noted that the impact of the failed road infrastructure goes beyond travel delays, as businesses suffer losses from delayed deliveries, increased transportation costs and vehicle damage. He added that farmers also face challenges transporting their produce to markets, while emergency cases involving patients, pregnant women and other vulnerable persons could be worsened by difficulties accessing the route. “The suffering on this road is unimaginable until one experiences it firsthand. Spending several hours on a single stretch of road is unacceptable in a country striving for economic growth and improved infrastructure,” Kahinde said. “Every minute lost on this road translates to lost productivity, wasted resources and unnecessary hardship for citizens.” WACI called on the Federal Government, Ondo State Government, the Federal Ministry of Works, the Senator representing Ondo North Senatorial District, Olajide Ipinsagba Emmanuel, and the Minister of Interior to urgently intervene and ensure the immediate commencement of work on the road. The group stressed that rehabilitating the road would boost economic activities, enhance security, facilitate movement of goods and restore public confidence in government’s commitment to infrastructure development. It urged relevant authorities to address all issues delaying the contractor’s mobilisation and ensure the project is completed within the shortest possible time. WACI reaffirmed its commitment to promoting transparency, accountability and responsive governance, adding that it would continue to advocate for citizens affected by abandoned or delayed public projects. items.title: Financing key to unlocking Africa’s energy potential – Jinapor
items.description: Ghana’s Energy and Green Transition Minister, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, says financing remains the biggest barrier to unlocking Africa’s energy potential. He said coordinated investment is needed to enable the continent to harness its energy resources to support technology, innovation, industrial growth and development. Dr Jinapor made the comments at the Stellenbosch Business School Alumni Association Thought Leadership Forum in Accra on Thursday, on the theme: “Technology-Powered Africa: Financing Sustainable Energy & Enterprise Transformation.” In a speech read on his behalf, Dr Jinapor said Africa’s energy sector is constrained by high capital costs linked to perceived risks, limited investment concentration and inadequate funding for energy access and infrastructure. He said public and private financiers, including G20-linked institutions and multilateral development banks, mobilised about US$345 billion for African energy projects between 2012 and 2021. He noted, however, that about 77 per cent of the funds went to only ten countries, including Egypt, Nigeria, South Africa, Angola, Morocco, Ghana, Uganda, Kenya and Ethiopia. Dr Jinapor urged African governments to prioritise strategic and collaborative financing to develop sustainable and resilient power systems and deepen regional electricity trade. He said the continent possessed significant energy resources, including strong solar potential and oil and gas reserves in countries such as Nigeria, Mozambique, Algeria and Senegal, yet more than half of Africans lacked access to electricity. The Minister said the challenge is particularly evident in clean cooking, where many households continue to rely on inefficient use of firewood, contributing to health problems, deforestation and waste. He said closing the gap between Africa’s energy potential and reality required effective funding structures, cost controls and government commitment. “With the right funding structures, cost controls, and government prioritisation, Africa can unlock its energy wealth to drive industrialization and poverty reduction. “African governments need to prioritise actions, capitalise economic transformation and manage energy resources as an economic base, not as a social handout plagued by subsidies and overspending,” he encouraged. Dr Jinapor called for sustained investment in transmission, distribution and energy storage, as well as stronger cross-border electricity trade. He said sharing excess power within the region could help countries “push it to countries ahead of us and improve energy security.” During a panel discussion, speakers said Africa needs to strengthen its technological and data capabilities, noting that access to capital alone would not address the continent’s development challenges. The speakers, drawn from academia, finance and industry, called for a common vision on sustainable development and collective action to achieve it. They cited mobile money as evidence that technology could succeed in Africa when adapted to local realities and urged similar approaches in sectors such as energy access.

Justice : Vers une nouvelle ère pour la médiation et l'arbitrage commercial au Maroc
items.description: À l’initiative conjointe de l’Amicale Hassania des Magistrats, du Club des Avocats au Maroc et de l'Institut Marocain de Médiation et d'Arbitrage, une journée d'étude et de débat a été organisée autour des modes alternatifs de règlement des différends (MARC). L'objectif : impulser une véritable dynamique d'adhésion aux mécanismes amiables. Dans un contexte de modernisation continue de l'appareil judiciaire du Royaume, les acteurs du monde du droit se sont réunis lors d'une journée de conférence-débat dédiée à la promotion de la médiation et de l'arbitrage. Cet événement, coorganisé par l’Amicale Hassania des Magistrats et le Club des Avocats au Maroc, entend accompagner l'évolution légale récente et ancrer une nouvelle culture du règlement des litiges. L'élément déclencheur de ce renouveau repose sur la loi n° 95-17 relative à la médiation et à l'arbitrage commercial. Ce texte est venu moderniser en profondeur ces deux mécanismes en les extirpant du Code de procédure civile pour leur offrir un régime juridique autonome, aligné sur les meilleurs standards internationaux. Cette dynamique franchit aujourd'hui un cap décisif grâce aux nouvelles orientations institutionnelles. Les intervenants ont notamment mis en lumière la récente circulaire du Conseil Supérieur du Pouvoir Judiciaire (CSPJ), datée du 5 mars dernier. En se fondant sur l'article 13 de la loi relative à l'organisation judiciaire, le CSPJ recommande vivement aux magistrats d'inviter et d'inciter les parties à privilégier les solutions amiables, tout particulièrement dans la sphère des litiges commerciaux. « Il ne s'agit plus seulement de disposer de textes modernes, mais de les mettre en œuvre sur le terrain par la promotion, la formation des acteurs, l'explication de ces mécanismes aux justiciables et la clarification de leurs bénéfices » , a souligné une intervenante lors des échanges. Présentée comme une opportunité majeure pour désengorger les tribunaux et offrir un climat des affaires plus serein, l'articulation entre modes alternatifs et justice traditionnelle a été au cœur des interventions. Pour les organisateurs, l'enjeu dépasse la simple réforme technique : il s'agit de bâtir un nouveau paradigme. En réunissant magistrats, avocats et médiateurs, cette rencontre a scellé une volonté de convergence visant à instaurer une relation harmonieuse et complémentaire entre la justice étatique et la justice privée. En plaçant la formation, la sensibilisation du justiciable et le partenariat interprofessionnel au centre des priorités, le corps judiciaire marocain entend donner un « souffle nouveau » à la résolution des conflits, plus agile et plus adapté aux exigences de l'économie moderne. items.title: ‘A growing economy with unemployed youth is a factory of frustration’ – Gideon Boako
items.description: The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has argued that Ghana’s improving macroeconomic indicators will mean little unless they translate into jobs, warning that economic growth without employment risks deepening public frustration. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, during discussions on the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, the Tano North MP said government cannot measure success solely by favourable fiscal and macroeconomic statistics while thousands of young people remain unemployed. Dr Boako maintained that the ultimate test of any economic recovery is whether it improves the lives of ordinary Ghanaians through employment, higher incomes and expanded economic opportunities. “A growing economy with unemployed youth is not growth but a factory of frustration,” he declared. According to him, while government has highlighted falling inflation, improving fiscal balances and stronger macroeconomic indicators, many young people continue to struggle to secure decent jobs despite completing their education. He argued that an economy that grows without creating employment risks widening inequality and undermining public confidence in economic reforms. Dr Boako said the country’s fiscal and economic policies should therefore be judged not only by headline growth figures but by their ability to stimulate private sector expansion, support entrepreneurship and create sustainable employment for the youth. “Economic growth must be reflected in jobs, businesses and improved living standards. If young people are still unable to find meaningful employment, then we cannot celebrate the numbers as though they tell the whole story,” he added.

items.title: ‘Economic indicators are green but social indicators are red’- Gideon Boako questions impact of recovery
items.description: The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has questioned whether Ghana’s reported economic recovery is translating into improved living conditions, insisting that the country’s social realities tell a different story from the government’s macroeconomic achievements. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, following Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson’s presentation of the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review, the Tano North MP said government has focused heavily on positive economic indicators while many households continue to face significant hardship. According to Dr Boako, improvements in inflation, fiscal balances and other macroeconomic indicators should not be mistaken for broad-based improvements in the welfare of Ghanaians. “Today in Ghana, economic indicators are green but social indicators are red,” he stated. He argued that rising youth unemployment, pressure on household incomes, the high cost of living and persistent economic hardship suggest that the benefits of the reported recovery have yet to reach many citizens. He said economic success should be measured not only by what appears in budget documents but also by the lived experiences of ordinary people. “Macroeconomic stability is important, but it is only a means to an end. The real objective is to improve the lives of Ghanaians. If families are still struggling to make ends meet and young people remain without jobs, then we must ask whether the recovery is truly inclusive,” Dr Boako said. He called on the government to complement fiscal consolidation with policies that accelerate job creation, boost private sector investment and improve social outcomes, arguing that sustainable economic progress must be reflected in both economic and human development indicators.

items.title: Mid-Year Budget Review: 40% underspend on capital expenditure raises questions over project delivery – Yaw Lartey
items.description: Partner at Deloitte, Yaw Appiah Lartey, has raised concerns over government’s capital expenditure performance, warning that a 40 per cent underspend could affect the implementation of major development projects. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, Mr Lartey said while there were some positive outcomes from savings in compensation and interest payments, the shortfall in capital spending remained a major concern. According to him, government had budgeted significantly for capital projects but failed to meet its spending targets during the period under review. He explained that programme expenditure was projected at GH¢158 billion for the first quarter, but actual expenditure resulted in an underspend of about 20 per cent. Mr Lartey noted that one of the positives was the reduction in compensation expenditure, which he attributed partly to improvements in payroll management and efforts to address issues such as ghost names. He said government’s actions in cleaning up the payroll helped save about GH¢3.4 billion. Another area where government recorded savings, he noted, was interest payments, where about GH¢6.9 billion was saved due to lower policy rates and cheaper borrowing conditions. “Government is borrowing at a much cheaper rate than it used to in the past, and that presents a positive development,” he said. However, Mr Lartey stressed that the major challenge was capital expenditure, which recorded an underspend of more than 40 per cent. He questioned the pace of implementation of government’s ambitious capital programme, particularly projects that require significant public investment. “On capital expenditure, we have an underspend of about 40 per cent. The question is how far we have progressed with the ambitious capital programme announced last year,” he said. Mr Lartey cautioned that delays in executing planned projects could affect infrastructure delivery, including roads and other key development initiatives. He, however, welcomed government’s approach of securing funding arrangements before beginning major projects, describing it as a positive shift that could prevent projects from being abandoned midway due to financing challenges. According to him, historically, some capital projects have suffered because construction began without guaranteed funding, resulting in delays and cost pressures. “Starting projects with funding secured means we do not have situations where projects begin and later get stuck because there is no money to continue,” he noted. Mr Lartey also highlighted concerns over revenue performance, stating that while government had managed to control some expenditure areas, revenue mobilisation remained a challenge. He said improving revenue collection would be critical to ensuring that government can finance its programmes and deliver the infrastructure expected by citizens.

items.title: African integration key to economic transformation, says Harakatiza Muungano President
items.description: The President of Harakatiza Muungano (Union Movement), Mr Kwame Danquah, has called for deeper political and economic integration across Sub-Saharan Africa, arguing that stronger regional cooperation is essential to accelerating industrialisation, reducing poverty and improving the continent’s global competitiveness. Addressing delegates at the Harakatiza Muungano conference in Accra, Mr Danquah said Africa must move beyond fragmented markets and colonial-era divisions to build a more united and prosperous future. He described the movement as one committed to promoting regional integration, removing barriers to trade and fostering seamless political and economic cooperation across the continent. According to him, Africa remains vulnerable to global economic shocks because of its heavy dependence on exporting primary commodities and limited intra-African trade. Citing the World Bank’s 2023 report, he said Africa’s combined Gross Domestic Product stands at about US$3 trillion, accounting for only a small share of the global economy, while the continent contributes just 3 per cent of global trade. He also noted that intra-African trade remains around 15 per cent, significantly lower than Europe and Asia. Mr Danquah warned that without bold structural reforms and accelerated industrialisation, African economies would continue to face external economic pressures and protectionist trade policies. “Unless African countries undertake bold structural reforms and accelerate industrialisation, they will remain exposed to external economic shocks and protectionist trade policies,” he said. He further highlighted Africa’s rapidly growing youth population, noting that the continent is projected to have about 2.5 billion people by 2050, with more than 60 per cent of Sub-Saharan Africa’s population under the age of 30. He said this presents an opportunity to harness a demographic dividend through investment in education, technology, skills development and infrastructure. The Harakatiza Muungano President also expressed concern over the growing number of young Africans risking dangerous migration routes in search of better opportunities abroad, describing it as a challenge that underscores the need for urgent economic reforms. “It is time to fix African economies through integration and reforms,” he stated. Mr Danquah proposed the establishment of an integrated African “Social Security Penta-Fund” to strengthen social protection and mobilise long-term investment capital. He said the initiative would comprise a mortgage finance scheme, medical insurance fund, education trust fund, social savings and investment scheme, and a provident and pensions fund to support both formal and informal sector workers. He concluded by urging participants to champion the vision of a politically united and economically integrated Sub-Saharan Africa capable of creating jobs, attracting investment and delivering sustainable prosperity. “Let us leave this conference motivated to spread the message to build a politically united and economically integrated sub-region which posterity will inherit as a land of prosperity, security and peaceful development,” he said.

items.title: Mame Makhtar Guèye : la constance d’un engagement (Par Abdoulaye DIALLO)
items.description: Il y a des combats à risque, ultrasensibles. Et si tu t’aventures à les porter, il faut s’attendre à tout et se préparer à en payer le prix fort. Parfois, c’est Dieu lui-même qui décide de t’éprouver pour mesurer ton degré de sincérité. C’est peut-être cela qui est arrivé à notre Mame Makhtar Guèye national, vice-président de l'ONG Jamra. Sa fille est citée dans une affaire de trafic international de cocaïne et d'actes contre nature, voilà que c’est lui qui se retrouve partout : sur les plateformes numériques, dans les sites d’information. Des éditions spéciales sont consacrées à l’affaire. Des chroniqueurs déchaînés. Une réputation salie. Une famille éclaboussée. Mais, contre toute attente, Mame Makhtar Guèye n’a pas cherché à se débiner. Il n’a pas fléchi d’un iota, restant droit dans ses bottes et décidé à affronter la situation, dans la douleur, mais avec dignité et responsabilité. « Il ne doit y avoir ni deux poids ni deux mesures. La justice doit être exemplaire dans le traitement de ce dossier », a réagi le vice-président de Jamra dans les colonnes de L’Observateur. Non seulement il refuse de prendre la défense de sa fille, mais il soutient également que cette épreuve ne remettra pas en cause son engagement. En digne continuateur de l’immense œuvre de son frère, Abdou Latif Guèye, brutalement arraché à notre affection le 6 avril 2008, Mame Makhtar estime que cette situation renforce même sa détermination. Il appelle les autorités judiciaires et les forces de sécurité à poursuivre leurs investigations « sans faiblesse ni complaisance ». Une posture admirable qui conforte et réconforte tous ceux qui l’ont connu et respecté. Voilà justement qui devait inspirer toutes les forces vives du pays pour apporter un soutien national à « Jamra » et à son vice-président. Mame Makhatar mène un combat noble. Et à ce titre, il mérite d’être soutenu et protégé, surtout dans ces moments difficiles. Il y va de l’intérêt supérieur du Sénégal et des Sénégalais. Rappelons-le : le combat que mène Jamra n’est pas sans dangers. Il exige du courage, beaucoup de courage, et de l’abnégation. S’y engager, c’est accepter de faire face à des lobbys puissants, dotés d’importants moyens financiers, qui profitent de la moindre fragilité pour vous discréditer et tenter de vous faire taire. Parfois, ce sont même des canaux insoupçonnés qui sont mis en branle pour vous atteindre et vous anéantir. Heureusement, le vice-président reste solide. Imperturbable, affichant sereinement sa volonté de poursuivre le noble combat, pour le bien de tous. Voilà pourquoi, plus que jamais, Mame Makhtar Guèye a besoin du soutien moral et psychologique des Sénégalais. Nous autres Sénégalais, pour lesquels il se bat depuis des années afin de nous préserver de ces fléaux modernes. Ces lobbys ont juré de détruire nos valeurs et de faire disparaître notre modèle de société. Il faudra encore plus de détermination et, sans doute, davantage de fermeté pour leur faire face. C’est une bataille qu’il faudra gagner. Mame Makhtar Guèye a montré la voie. Il est sur la bonne voie. À nous de le suivre et de le renforcer. Et en première ligne de cette union sacrée autour de ces vaillants défenseurs du Sénégal et de ses valeurs, la presse doit figurer en bonne place. Elle doit rester particulièrement vigilante afin d’échapper à toute tentative de manipulation. Encore une fois, cette affaire dépasse Mame Makhtar Guèye et sa famille. Elle s’inscrit dans un combat plus large : celui d’un pays qui refuse de se voir imposer un modèle de société et qui entend défendre sa propre vision du monde ainsi que les valeurs auxquelles il est attaché. abdoulaye.diallo@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Economic gains are driven by IMF programme not superior economic management – Dr Boako
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Tano North, Dr Gideon Boako, has rejected claims made by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson that Ghana’s recent economic gains are solely the result of superior economic management. The legislator believes that the recovery has largely been driven by the IMF-supported programme and reforms initiated by the previous administration. According to him, the Finance Minister’s attribution of the gains to the current government’s policies amounts to “attribution bias” and fails to acknowledge the foundation that was laid before the change in government. “We have come from somewhere,” Dr Boako said, stressing that the minister must recognise the processes and policy decisions that preceded the current administration. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, he argued that while the government deserves credit for maintaining some of the policies it inherited, it cannot claim exclusive responsibility for the country’s improving macroeconomic indicators. “The decision not to change what you inherited is itself a decision. If it produces good results, it should be commended. But whatever has brought us here is multi-causal, not mono-causal,” he stated. Dr Boako cited the National Development Planning Commission’s assessment of Ghana’s IMF-supported programme, which attributed improvements to fiscal consolidation, expenditure rationalisation, monetary policy tightening, debt restructuring, reforms to restore confidence in the foreign exchange market and measures to strengthen reserve accumulation. He said the report clearly demonstrates that the country’s economic gains are the result of multiple policy interventions rather than the actions of the current administration alone. The MP also questioned the durability of the economic recovery, arguing that weak domestic revenue mobilisation remains a major concern. He noted that although the government had targeted an 18 per cent revenue-to-GDP ratio, it achieved only about 15.5 to 15.7 per cent in 2025, figures he said remain below the level inherited by the current administration. READ ALSO: Ghana’s IMF bailout programme to end next week after final review – Ato Forson Dr Boako further claimed that revenue shortfalls persisted into 2026, affecting major tax handles, including PAYE, corporate income tax, customs duties and the Growth and Sustainability Levy. He also accused the Finance Minister of understating the 2026 revenue figures during the Mid-Year Budget Review, arguing that the budget appendices reveal a larger revenue challenge. According to him, falling revenues have forced government spending below target, raising concerns about the state’s ability to finance critical infrastructure and essential public services. “We need to ask ourselves whether we want to achieve impressive economic indicators at the expense of delivering roads, power, water, irrigation, industrial parks and other essential services to the people,” he said.

items.title: Transferts : Mady Camara placé sur le marché par le PAOK Salonique, plusieurs clubs européens à l’affût
items.description: Ça sent la fin entre Mady Camara et le PAOK Salonique. Auteur d'une première saison convaincante sous les couleurs du club Grec, l'international guinéen serait sur le départ lors de cette fenêtre de transferts, malgré la volonté du club de le conserver. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, les dirigeants du PAOK souhaitaient prolonger le contrat du milieu de terrain de 29 ans. Mais face au refus du joueur du Syli National de parapher un nouveau bail, le club grec aurait décidé de le placer sur le marché des transferts. Sous contrat jusqu'en 2027, Mady Camara disposerait désormais d'un bon de sortie. Le PAOK serait prêt à étudier les offres pour son joueur, notamment en raison de son salaire élevé, tout en fixant un prix de départ jugé abordable. Les prétendants ne manqueraient d'ailleurs pas. Toujours selon FootMercato, l’international guinéen aurait déjà décliné une offre de Cruzeiro, au Brésil, privilégiant vraisemblablement un maintien sur la scène européenne. En Espagne, Getafe et le Rayo Vallecano se seraient renseignés sur la situation du milieu guinéen. En Allemagne, Fribourg et Mayence suivraient également le dossier avec attention. Pour l'heure, aucun accord n'a été officialisé entre le PAOK Salonique et un club intéressé. Le dossier reste donc au stade des discussions et des rumeurs de transferts. Sadjo Bah L’article Transferts : Mady Camara placé sur le marché par le PAOK Salonique, plusieurs clubs européens à l'affût est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Le procureur de la CPI Karim Khan révoqué sur fond d’allégations d’agressions sexuelles
items.description: Lors d'un vote a bulletin secret pendant une reunion exceptionnelle et a huis clos au siege de l'ONU a New York, le 24 juillet, l'assemblee des 125 etats membres de la Cour penale internationale (CPI) a decide de relever le procureur general Karim Khan de ses fonctions. Pour valider la decision, 63 votes etaient necessaires. De fait, 82 etats membres ont vote pour la fin du mandat du magistrat britannique de 56 ans, l'Assemblee l'accusant de « faute grave » et de « manquement grave aux devoirs de sa charge ». Les resultats du vote font aussi etat de 13 pays favorables au maintien du procureur et de 15 abstentions. La destitution a ete approuvee deux ans apres que soient rendues publiques des accusations d'agressions sexuelles a l'encontre de Karim Khan. Selon Tayab Ali, le chef de l'equipe juridique du procureur de la CPI, un panel judiciaire avait determine « a l'unanimite » que les conclusions du Bureau des services de controle interne des Nations unies « n'etablissaient pas de faute ou de manquement a ses obligations de la part de M. Khan dans le cadre juridique pertinent ». Il a indique dans ce contexte que les « graves consequences » que la decision suscitait allaient bien au-dela du cas de Karim Khan, dans la mesure ou l'independance de la CPI « repose sur la protection de ses representants elus contre toute destitution par des procedures politiques, proceduralement inequitables ou incompatibles avec les conclusions d'organes judiciaires independants ». « Escalade des tentatives », selon l'accusatrice du procureur ; absence de preuves, selon son avocat Dans une recente interview sur CNN, l'accusatrice de Karim Khan, une jeune femme presentee comme une avocate originaire de Malaisie appelee Sarah, a parle d'une « escalade des tentatives » d'attouchements sexuels, alleguant qu'il etait « impossible qu'il y ait consentement quand il existe un tel desequilibre de pouvoir. Ce que beaucoup de gens ne comprennent pas est que M. Khan n'etait pas seulement mon patron, mais le patron de tout le monde ». Pour l'avocat du procureur de la CPI, celui-ci a ete destitue « par un vote executif alors qu'il etait sous sanctions et que la Cour subissait une immense pression politique », indiquant que la decision de l'Assemblee ne tenait pas compte « des preuves ni des conclusions de la seule decision judiciaire rendue en la matiere ». Karim Khan « n'a jamais eu la possibilite d'etre entendu equitablement », a affirme Tayab Ali, ajoutant que la decision avait ete prise « au mepris des conclusions des juges independants qui ont examine l'integralite du dossier de preuve ». « Karim Khan va contester la legalite et l'equite de la decision par tous les mecanismes juridiques disponibles », a-t-il fait savoir. Apres le vote, la CPI a annonce que le bureau de Karim Khan serait desormais dirige par les procureures adjointes Nazhat Shameen Khan et Mame Mandiaye Niang. La revocation de Karim Khan declenche immediatement un processus electoral pour nommer un nouveau procureur de la CPI, mais le vote n'est pas attendu avant l'annee prochaine. Reaction de la Russie, des etats-Unis et d'Israel La porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a declare qu'elle ne voulait pas « entrer dans les details des perversions sexuelles » du procureur de la CPI. « Mais nous devons parler du fait qu'une structure quasi legale a emerge dans le monde, qui, par son existence meme, detruit la notion de loi et d'ordre », a-t-elle assene. Tommy Pigott, porte-parole de la diplomatie americaine, a ecrit sur X le 24 juillet que « Karim Khan est un exemple emblematique d'une CPI corrompue et de l'abus de l'autorite qu'elle pretend detenir. C'est une bonne chose qu'il soit parti, mais il n'etait qu'un rouage mineur dans cette institution irremediablement corrompue ». Pour sa part, le chef de la diplomatie israelienne, Gideon Sa'ar, s'est rejoui d'un limogeage « longtemps attendu » de Karim Khan qu'il a qualifie de « corrompu qui s'etait empresse de demander des mandats d'arret scandaleux » contre des officiels israeliens « pour tenter de detourner l'attention d'une faute grave qu'il craignait de voir reveler ». Pour rappel, Karim Khan a emis des mandats d'arret contre le Premier ministre israelien Benjamin Netanyahou et son ministre de la Defense de l'epoque, Yoav Gallant, en 2024, qui lui ont attire les foudres d'Israel et des etats-Unis, qui ont emis des sanctions a son encontre.

items.title: Naqvi, Bugti review Balochistan's security situation, vow stronger counter-terrorism measures
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited Quetta on Saturday, where he chaired a high-level meeting with Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti to review the province’s law and order situation. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Interior, the chief minister briefed the meeting on the overall security situation, ongoing measures and the provincial government’s future strategy. The statement said the meeting decided to further enhance the professional capacity of the Counter-Terrorism Force and Balochistan police, while expediting the implementation of measures aimed at strengthening the provincial police. It said the interior ministry assured the provincial government of its full cooperation in providing the resources required for the purpose. “The federal government will continue to provide all possible support for sustainable peace in Balochistan,” Naqvi was quoted as saying. He also stressed the need for the immediate and effective implementation of the province’s peace restoration plan and called for making “full use” of the experience of former Balochistan police chiefs in formulating the law and order strategy. The interior minister said modern technology, improved intelligence and coordinated action were essential in the fight against terrorism, adding that the “federation and the Balochistan government were moving forward in complete unity and coordination to establish peace”. Bugti said the government would remain “one step ahead” in the fight against terrorism and would not come under any pressure. He reiterated that the writ of the state would be established “at all costs” and that no space would be left for terrorists, the statement said. The chief minister said providing young people with education, skills, employment opportunities and opportunities for positive activities remained the government’s top priority, adding that promoting merit would help restore the confidence of the youth. Bugti added that peace, development and prosperity were closely linked and pledged to pursue progress on both fronts simultaneously, adding that the implementation of law and order measures and development projects would be accelerated with the federation’s support. Naqvi’s visit came amid heightened security concerns in Balochistan following a spate of major terrorist attacks earlier this month, which prompted a series of counter-terrorism operations across the province. Among the counter-terrorism efforts was Operation Shaban , in which 91 terrorists were killed between July 5 and July 16, according to security sources cited by state media. This took the tally of terrorists eliminated in operations across the province during the period to 129.

items.title: Burkina/Contrats d’objectifs 2026: le ministère de la Santé enregistre un taux d’exécution de 50,76 % à mi-parcours
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a reçu, ce samedi 25 juillet 2026, le Camarade ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, dans le cadre de l’évaluation de la mise en œuvre, au 30 juin 2026, des contrats d’objectifs des ministres. Au terme de cette évaluation, le contrat d’objectifs du Camarade ministre de la Santé affiche un taux d’exécution physique global de 50,76 %. Ce résultat traduit les progrès accomplis dans la mise en œuvre des actions prioritaires destinées à améliorer l’offre de soins et à renforcer la protection de la santé des populations. Présentant les principales réalisations de son département, le Camarade ministre de la Santé a notamment évoqué la poursuite de l’apurement du passif social au sein de la Gestion des structures de santé publiques (AGSP). Le taux de mise en œuvre de ce processus s’établit à 60 %, avec pour objectif son achèvement d’ici à la fin du mois d’octobre. Le premier semestre de l’année a également été marqué par le renforcement des infrastructures sanitaires, avec l’inauguration de quatre nouveaux centres d’hémodialyse à Banfora, Dédougou, Dori et Fada N’Gourma. Ces infrastructures permettent de rapprocher davantage les soins spécialisés des populations. À ces réalisations s’ajoutent l’inauguration de 18 Centres de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) et la mise en service de 49 postes de santé communautaire. Ces nouvelles infrastructures contribuent à améliorer l’accès aux soins de plus de 150 000 Burkinabè. Sous la coordination du Camarade Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, le ministère de la Santé a également enregistré des avancées majeures dans le domaine des soins hautement spécialisés, avec la réalisation, en février 2026, de deux transplantations rénales. Cette performance confirme l’entrée du Burkina Faso dans le cercle restreint des pays de la sous-région capables de réaliser ce type d’intervention. Parallèlement, le renforcement des plateaux techniques des hôpitaux, aussi bien à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso que dans les centres hospitaliers régionaux, contribue à améliorer l’équité dans l’accès aux soins spécialisés. Les performances enregistrées au Centre hospitalier universitaire de Tengandogo dans les domaines de la chirurgie cardiaque et de la chirurgie thoracique illustrent également cette dynamique. Dans le domaine de la prévention, le Camarade ministre a relevé les résultats obtenus lors de la première campagne de chimioprévention du paludisme saisonnier. À cette occasion, plus de 1,3 million d’enfants âgés de 3 à 59 mois ont bénéficié gratuitement de médicaments préventifs. Le ministère de la Santé a, par ailleurs, poursuivi ses efforts de prestation en services essentiels de santé et de nutrition et plus de cinq millions de femmes et d’enfants en ont bénéficié jusque même dans les zones à fort défi sécuritaire. Au regard de ces résultats, le Camarade Premier ministre a salué les performances enregistrées par le ministre de la Santé. Il l’a encouragé à poursuivre cette dynamique et lui a donné de nouvelles orientations en vue d’accélérer la mise en œuvre des actions engagées. items.title: Nigéria : Royal Air Maroc menacée de suspension, Air Algérie citée comme alternative
items.description: Le service de la Royal Air Maroc (RAM) est sévèrement critiqué par la direction de l’aviation civile du Nigeria qui menace de suspendre la compagnie aérienne marocaine. La compagnie aérienne marocaine est mise en garde qu'elle pourrait perdre sa position dans le plus peuplé des pays d’Afrique, d'autant plus que des alternatives existent, Air Algérie entre autres. La compagnie aérienne nationale dessert Abuja depuis avril 2025 via Douala au Cameroun dans le cadre de son redéploiement en Afrique et à l'international, avec l'objectif de faire de l'aéroport d'Alger, un hub entre le continent et le reste du monde. Des défaillances en cascade de la RAM au Nigeria Michael Achimugu est le directeur des affaires publiques et de la protection des clients à la NCAA (Nigeria civil aviation authority). Sur la plateforme X, il a retenu plusieurs griefs contre la RAM, qu’il a tenue pour responsable, “depuis très longtemps”, des infractions liées aux bagages, de la mauvaise gestion des passagers et de la grande inefficacité des procédures de résolution des litiges concernant les passagers nigérians. La compagnie marocaine a été sanctionnée pour la première fois en 2025 pour des infractions liées à la protection des consommateurs. “On aurait pu s’attendre à des améliorations très significatives dans la manière avec laquelle elle traite les réclamations des passagers nigérians”, écrit le responsable. Malheureusement, déplore-t-il, malgré le soutien “sans faille” de la NCAA, “la manière dont ces problèmes sont traités ne s’est guère améliorée”. Michael Achimugu relève que “les bagages continuent d’être égarés sans que les passagers concernés en soient informés en temps utile, les indemnités d’urgence ne sont pas versées de manière systématique, et les réclamations ne sont généralement traitées qu’après forte pression de la NCAA”. La RAM aux responsables nigérians : “Faites ce que vous voulez !” Le responsable nigérian dénonce particulièrement l’ “insolence inacceptable” de la RAM vis-à-vis des invitations de la NCAA. Et il donne des exemples. Le directeur de la RAM au Nigeria reste à Lagos et refuse d’assister aux réunions à Abuja. La veille d’une réunion, la compagnie marocaine a envoyé un mail “à la hâte” pour indiquer que les dossiers sont en cours de traitement, avant d'envoyer son représentant à Abuja “qui n’a pas le pouvoir de résoudre les dossiers ni de prendre des engagements.” Le dernier incident en date a eu lieu le 23 juillet. Alors que la NCAA a exprimé son mécontentement face à ce “mépris incessant” envers les passagers nigérians et l’Autorité, le directeur de la RAM au Nigeria a répondu par un insolent “faites ce que vous voulez.” La NCAA “ne se laissera jamais rabaisser à un tel niveau de mépris éhonté et de non-respect des règles”, a tonné Michael Achimugu. “Les passagers dont les bagages ont été retardés, de manière tout à fait injuste et inutile, sont des clients fidèles qui paient pour ce service” et “les compagnies aériennes internationales doivent respecter des accords bilatéraux de services (BASA), ainsi que l’obligation fondamentale d’assurer un service de qualité aux passagers”, a-t-il rappelé. La suspension de la RAM évoquée, Air Algérie parmi les alternatives Le responsable a aussi évoqué la possibilité de la suspension de la compagnie marocaine au Nigeria. “Des mesures strictes seront prises à l’encontre de cette compagnie aérienne et le ministère fera pression pour que Royal Air Maroc cesse ses activités au Nigeria jusqu’à ce qu’elle s’engage à mieux traiter les passagers nigérians”, a-t-il écrit. La RAM ne devrait pas agir ainsi et faire en sorte “comme si les règles n’existaient pas” car la compagnie n’est pas seule sur le marché et des alternatives existent, parmi lesquelles la compagnie aérienne algérienne. “Il n’y a aucune destination desservie par RAM pour laquelle les voyageurs ne disposent pas d’alternatives avec Air Algérie , EgyptAir et Ethiopian Airlines”, a rappelé Achimugu. “Mon département adoptera une position très ferme sur cette question, et Royal Air Maroc cessera de prendre pour acquise la relation dont le Maroc a bénéficié avec le Nigeria et les Nigérians”, a promis le responsable, assurant que son institution veillera “cette fois-ci à ce que des sanctions plus sévères soient infligées à Royal Air Maroc”. “La mission qui nous a été confiée sera menée à bien sans crainte”, a-t-il conclu. The airline, Royal Air Maroc, has for the longest time, been the biggest culprit when it comes to baggage infractions, poor passenger handling, and extremely poor resolution processes when dealing with Nigerian passengers. Having been sanctioned – for the first time ever – for… — Michael Achimugu (@mikeachimugu01) July 23, 2026 L’article Nigéria : Royal Air Maroc menacée de suspension, Air Algérie citée comme alternative est apparu en premier sur TSA .

PML-N's 'gift': Buses promised by Maryam reach AJK as election commission warns against violating electoral code
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: E-buses announced by the PML-N as a “gift” arrived in Muzaffarabad on Saturday as the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission warned against violating the code of conduct for election campaigns. The AJK Election Commission warned that it would not allow any individual or institution to violate the code of conduct, a day after former prime minister Nawaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced development schemes, including the “gift” of 10 e-buses at election rallies in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur. CM Maryam confirmed on Saturday afternoon that the green buses had arrived in the regional capital, sharing a video that showed several of the vehicles bearing posters with her picture. The PML-N’s Friday announcement had not gone well with the PPP, which described it as “political bribery”. It then approached the Election Commission, urging it to take notice of what it termed a violation of the election code of conduct. Subsequently, an Election Commission spokesperson said federal and provincial ministers were free to participate in electioneering in AJK but could not use official protocol, government resources or the state machinery for electoral purposes. The spokesperson warned that the announcement of any new development scheme, financial package, public facility or welfare project during the election campaign would amount to a violation of the code of conduct. Any vehicles, equipment, relief goods or other facilities sent by the federal or provincial governments during the election period would be confiscated and action taken in accordance with the law, the statement added. The spokesperson urged all ministers, candidates and political parties to strictly observe the code of conduct to ensure free, fair and transparent elections and maintain public confidence in the electoral process. Meanwhile, AJK Secretary Information Muhammad Rashid Hanif and Director Information Tariq Jamil Durrani urged journalists and media organisations to ensure responsible, impartial and professional coverage of the elections. In a joint message, they called on the media to publish only verified and balanced information, avoid rumours and inflammatory content, and adhere to the Election Commission’s code of conduct and journalistic ethics. They also urged users of social media platforms to refrain from sharing unverified or misleading material that could undermine the electoral process or disturb public order. PPP accuses PML-N of ‘political bribery’ Separately, PPP Secretary General Nayyer Hussain Bukhari met with AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Saturday over the issue of pre-poll development schemes. He urged the CEC to take notice of the Punjab government’s decision to hand over 10 electric buses bearing the photographs of CM Maryam to the AJK administration. He said the PPP considered the act as “political bribery” and alleged that the PML-N was trying to “buy the AJK elections” by using tax money of the people of Punjab. “After the announcement of the election schedule, any such step by any executive amounts to a clear violation of election laws,” he asserted. Bukhari questioned whether the buses were purchased “from the account of Jati Umra”, and asked the CEC to take notice of the matter. He also submitted a request for issuance of a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the PPP to run a “motivation service” in connection with the party manifesto and election campaign in AJK, and urged the CEC to decide early on the party’s appeal. Matters related to the AJK general elections 2026, the code of conduct, and permission letters required for political parties also came under discussion. In a statement, PPP Central Spokesperson Shazia Marri said Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari was striving for a bright and empowered future for every Kashmiri. She said the PPP chairman had raised the slogan of the right to rule, right to property and right to employment for the people of Kashmir, adding “this is not a crime”. Marri asked PML-N to present its plan of action for Kashmir to the people instead of attacking political allies. “The people of Kashmir do not want allegations by political parties; they want solutions to their problems,” she said. She said Nawaz was repeating the same old narrative on which he “could not deliver despite being in power three times”.

items.title: Licenciements dans les hôpitaux publics : Les agents de sécurité privée annoncent une mobilisation
items.description: Le conflit autour des licenciements d'agents de sécurité privée dans les hôpitaux publics connaît un nouvel épisode. Le Syndicat national des agents de sécurité privée, de nettoyage et de restauration a annoncé l'organisation, la semaine prochaine, d'un sit-in national devant le siège du ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale à Rabat, afin de dénoncer ce qu'il qualifie de « poursuite des licenciements arbitraires » visant les agents de sécurité privée. L'organisation réclame également la réintégration de l'ensemble des salariés licenciés. Dans un communiqué publié vendredi 24 juillet, le syndicat, affilié à la Confédération démocratique du travail (CDT), affirme qu'une décision ministérielle est à l'origine du licenciement de dizaines de travailleuses et de travailleurs. Selon lui, cette mesure a entraîné de lourdes répercussions sociales et familiales, laissant de nombreuses personnes sans emploi. Il estime que la persistance de cette situation traduit un manque de sérieux dans le traitement d'un dossier qu'il présente comme revêtant des dimensions à la fois sociales et humaines. L'organisation syndicale indique par ailleurs que son bureau national avait obtenu, ces derniers mois, des engagements portant sur la réintégration des agents licenciés. Toutefois, ces promesses, précise le communiqué, ne se sont pas traduites par des mesures concrètes, ce qui a conduit le syndicat à durcir son action en appelant à une mobilisation nationale. Cette manifestation, explique le syndicat, vise à défendre le droit au travail des agents de sécurité privée, à préserver leur stabilité professionnelle et sociale et à contester les décisions qui, selon lui, conduisent à leur exclusion du marché de l’emploi et à la perte de leur unique source de revenus. Enfin, le syndicat annonce qu'il précisera ultérieurement la date et l'heure de ce sit-in national. Il réitère, dans le même temps, son exigence d'une réintégration immédiate de l'ensemble des agents licenciés dans leurs postes. The post Licenciements dans les hôpitaux publics : Les agents de sécurité privée annoncent une mobilisation appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: École : le redoublement, une grande équation (Par Daouda MANÉ)
items.description: En 2010, les inspecteurs de l’enseignement moyen secondaire, au cours d’un atelier de 3 jours (du 3 et 6 août 2010) – qui avait pour but de plancher sur les questions du curriculum, de l’évaluation des compétences, l’amélioration de l’enseignement des sciences, mais surtout celle relative à leur corps -, s’étaient fixés un objectif : faire baisser le taux de redoublement en-deçà de 5% contre un objectif de 7% du Pdef. À cet effet, ils se sont dotés d’un plan d’actions dont les activités phares consisteraient à prendre en charge, à travers les cellules pédagogiques, les élèves à faible niveau dans la soirée des jours non ouvrables (mercredi et samedi), cela, dès octobre 2010. Le plan d’actions était alors évalué à « au moins 10 milliards de FCfa, de 2010 à 2015 ». Ce qui, de l’avis du coordonnateur national des inspecteurs de spécialité d’alors, Masseck Birame Seck, par ailleurs Chef de la division des enseignements-apprentissages à la Direction de l’enseignement moyen secondaire général (Demsg), ne représente rien face au coût actuel du redoublement pour l’État. Car, en plus d’impacter négativement sur la qualité, le redoublement coûte cher à l’État. En 2009, l’évaluation de la phase II du Pdef a montré que le taux de redoublement est très élevé : 16% dans le moyen pour un objectif de 10% et 19,28% dans le secondaire. Selon le rapport national sur la situation de l’Éducation, sur 472.661 élèves du moyen, il y a eu 75.625 redoublants, soit 15,99% de l’effectif. En réalité, au Sénégal, le taux de redoublement est resté structurellement élevé. Avec l’abandon, il reste un défi majeur pour l’efficacité du système éducatif. Il tourne autour de 12 à 15 voire 20%. Autrement dit, le redoublement demeure un levier sur lequel le système éducatif sénégalais peine à agir de manière significative, en dépit de la hausse des taux de scolarisation. Le coût financier est énorme pour l’État et les familles. En 2010, expliquait Masseck Birame Seck, compte tenu du coût moyen d’un élève du cycle moyen qui était de 51.471 FCfa, le redoublement coûtait annuellement 3.893.494.375 FCfa à l’État. Au secondaire, le coût moyen de l’élève était de 185.585 FCfa. D’après ses estimations, à l’horizon 2015, « le redoublement coûtera à l’État, dans le moyen, 32.585.827.389 FCfa et 45.889.215.597 FCfa dans le secondaire, soit un total de 78.475.042.986 FCfa entre 2010 et 2015 dans le sous-secteur de l’enseignement moyen secondaire. Des calculs, a précisé M. Seck, qui ont été effectués sur la base des taux constants de redoublement par niveau, le coût constant de l’élève et de l’évolution des effectifs et qui ne tenaient pas compte du coût de l’apprenant au niveau des parents. Entre 2012 et 2015, par exemple, le redoublement et l’abandon (ils vont souvent de pair), ont représenté environ 13,72% des dépenses d’éducation. (Cf. Wikipedia). Au-delà du coût financier, le redoublement augmente les risques d’abandon scolaire parce qu’il démotive, n’améliore guère les performances et peut fragiliser la confiance de l’élève. Conséquence : ses ambitions scolaires, sa perte de l’estime en soi sont réduites, fait remarquer la confemen. « Le redoublement est l’un des facteurs explicatifs du retard de la scolarisation, car un élève qui redouble monopolise une place qui aurait pu être attribuée à un nouvel élève. Ce qui s’avère extrêmement pénalisant pour l’atteinte de la scolarisation universelle. (Cf. Confemen : Le redoublement au Sénégal : Facteurs de qualité ou entrave à la scolarisation universelle). Pourtant, des pays étaient arrivés à réduire très sensiblement voire à presque éliminer le redoublement. C’est le cas de l’Égypte (5%), de l’Allemagne (2%), du Ghana (3%), de la France (5%). Avec une volonté politique affirmée, sûr que le Sénégal peut inverser la tendance. daouda.mane@lesoleil.sn
